subject: Renewal: Onramp & migration plan for reserved GPU increase
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily@acme.ai>
Cc: hiro_tanaka <hiro@redwood.com>, chloe_martin <chloe@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: Onramp & migration plan for reserved GPU increase

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our renewal, ACME is on track to increase your Dedicated reserved pool from 16 -> 48 A100-equivalent GPUs and extend the term to 12 months. I attached a short summary that outlines the proposed commercial terms and the recommended delivery cadence.

Highlights: 
- Capacity: +32 GPUs in a new reserved pool (region: us-west-2)
- Throughput commitment: baseline target 2,500 tokens/sec for API-bound traffic; monitoring and credits for regression in first 90 days
- Term: 12 months (renewal price as in attached summary)

Proposed high-level plan for rollout/cutover (draft):
- Pre-cutover prep: kernel/profile selection and quantization profile pinning (we'll do an offline test mix)
- Canary: shift 10% traffic to new pool with 4h steady-state windows, progressive ramp to 50% over 48h
- Full cutover: target week of Jun 29 - Jul 2 (dependent on PO and security review)
- Rollback: immediate fallback to existing pool if >3% error rate or P95 latency breach for >30 minutes

Attachments: acme_renewal_summary_v2.pdf (proposal & commercial); will follow up with a cutover runbook and owner matrix.

Can you confirm: procurement timeline for a PO, any procurement/finance lead I should loop in, and whether the proposed cutover week looks feasible on your side? Also call out any additional security/compliance checks required for the new pool.

Thanks —
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0137

From: Emily Chen <emily@acme.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Onramp & migration plan for reserved GPU increase

Thanks Sergio — this looks promising. A couple of things we need clarified before procurement signs off:

1) Canary/rollback specifics: does Redwood have a small-footprint traffic-splitting capability at the gateway level so we can target a subset of customers? We prefer targeting sandbox and a percentage of low-risk traffic.
2) Throughput SLA: you quoted 2,500 tokens/sec. Is that set per-pool or per-tenant? What's your enforcement/credit calculation if we see degradation during business hours?
3) Audit/logging: we need confirmation that object-level audit logs and request tracing for the new pool will be stored for 90 days as per our policy.

Cc’ing procurement so they can flag timing. I have a calendar constraint the week of Jun 29 but we can accommodate a phased ramp earlier if needed.

Sergio / team —

Draft cutover runbook and canary plan below. I attached cutover_runbook.xlsx (action matrix + play-by-play). Summary version for Emily/procurement: 

Canary & migration proposal (operationally precise):
- Pre-cutover (T-7 to T-3 days): 
  - Kernel/profile pinning + quantization profile locked on a staging copy of the model (owner: Hiro)
  - KV cache warming: run replay workload for 6h prior to canary start (owner: Chloe)
  - Capacity smoke tests: throughput soak to validate 75% baseline capacity (owner: Infra SRE)
- Canary (T-2 to T-1): 
  - Day 0: route 10% production traffic to new pool for 4h steady-state; verify error rate, latency P95, and tail latency metrics
  - Day 1: if metrics stable, ramp to 25% for 6h; Day 2: 50% for 12h; if all checks pass schedule full cutover window
- Full cutover (target week Jun 29 - Jul 2): progressive traffic shift outside business-hours where possible; burst capacity enabled for first 72h

Rollback / abort conditions (immediate rollback to previous pool):
- sustained error rate > 3% over a 30m window
- P95 latency > target (currently 220ms) for 30m and trending upward
- 3x expected cost delta spike (unexpected resource behaviour)

Monitoring & telemetry: 
- Per-request traces + object-level audit logs (retention 90d) — we will provide the S3 bucket path and IAM role before cutover
- Canary dashboard: latency percentiles, error rate, token throughput; automated Slack alert to on-call SRE if threshold breached

Owners & runbook references (see attached):
- Cutover owner: Laura Bennett (eng ops)
- SRE lead (infra): Hiro Tanaka
- Customer success touchpoint: Chloe Martin

I'll add timing for the pre-cutover dry-run in the attached workbook. If ACME wants we can run a customer-facing smoke test (sandbox users only) two days ahead.

--
Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions & Deployments, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

- Cutover week target: Jun 29 - Jul 2. Pre-cutover dry-run: Jun 24 (sandbox smoke test)
- DocuSign (final contract + amendment) ready: https://www.docusign.com/prepare/abcdef1234567890
- HubSpot deal for internal tracking: https://app.redwood.com/deals/ACME-1257

If procurement can issue a PO aligned to the pricing in the summary, we’ll schedule the dry-run and lock owners. Please confirm preferred final cutover date — if Jun 29 is OK we’ll block the calendar and begin pre-cutover tasks next week.

Procurement has reviewed and we can issue PO# 678934 for the 32 GPU add-on. We are provisionally approving the Jun 29 cutover window. Attached PO will follow as ACME_PO_678934.pdf once legal completes a quick review (expected Monday).

A couple of final asks before cutover:
